english.topic: Power cut stories and word meanings
english.goal: I can retell a story in order, show feelings without words, and work out what a word means from the sentence.

learn.title: Tell it in order
learn.text: When we retell a story, we say the important parts in the same order as the story. Order words help us.

learn.title: Be a story detective
learn.text: To answer a question about a story, go back to the story and look for clues in the words and pictures. Don't guess!

learn.title: Feelings without words
learn.text: Our face, eyes and body can show how we feel, even when we don't speak. This is called body language.

learn.title: One word, two meanings
learn.text: Some words have two meanings. Read the whole sentence to find out which meaning fits. A bat can be an animal, or a stick for hitting a ball!

learn.title: Word beginnings and endings
learn.text: A prefix goes at the start of a word. A suffix goes at the end. They change the meaning. un- means not. -ful means full of. -ly tells us how.

practice.title: The night the lights went out
practice.storyTitle: The Night the Lights Went Out
practice.text:
It was a hot evening in Dubai. Maryam and her little brother Omar were reading books in their flat.
First, the lights flickered. Click! Everything went dark. The fan stopped and the TV went quiet. Omar felt worried, so he held Maryam's hand.
Next, Dad found a torch in the kitchen drawer. Mum put a candle in a glass jar and placed it safely on the table.
Then the family sat together on the sofa. Dad told funny stories and they made shadow animals on the wall.
Finally, the lights came back on. Everyone cheered! "That was the best power cut ever!" laughed Omar.
practice.prompt: Read the story. Tap the 4 order words.
practice.missHint: Look for a word that tells us when something happened.

practice.title: What happened first?
practice.prompt: Put the story in order. Tap what happened first.

maths.topic: Odd and even, and units of time
maths.goal: I can tell if a number is odd or even, and I can order units of time from shortest to longest.

learn.title: Sharing into two
learn.text: An even number can be shared equally between 2 people. An odd number can't, because 1 is always left over.

learn.title: Look at the last digit
learn.text: For any number, just look at the ones digit at the end. 34 ends in 4, so it is even. 57 ends in 7, so it is odd.

learn.title: Odd and even in the UAE
learn.text: The UAE has 7 emirates, and 7 is odd. A class of 26 children can make 2 equal teams of 13, because 26 is even. If there are 27, one child is left over!

learn.title: Units of time
learn.text: We measure time in seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years. A second is very short. A year is very long!
learn.big: second → minute → hour → day → week → month → year

learn.title: How they fit together
learn.text: A car trip from Abu Dhabi to Dubai takes about 1 hour. A flight from Dubai to London takes about 7 hours. The flight is longer!
learn.extra: 24 hours = 1 day · 7 days = 1 week · 12 months = 1 year

gp.topic: How far does our food travel?
gp.goal: I can say where some of my food comes from and explain how it travels to our table.

learn.title: Food comes from many places
learn.text: Some of our food grows here in the UAE. Some comes from countries far away, and travels a long way to reach us.

learn.title: From the farm to our table
learn.text: Food is grown on a farm. A truck takes it away. A ship or plane carries it across the world. Then it goes to the market or shop, and finally to our home.
learn.big: farm → truck → ship or plane → market → our table

learn.title: Near or far?
learn.text: Food from near us has a short journey. Food from other countries has a long journey.

compare.title: 🏠 Near
lines: grown or caught in the UAE

compare.title: 🌍 Far
lines: long trip by ship or plane

learn.title: Why do some foods travel far?
learn.text: Some foods can't grow in the UAE. Bananas, coffee and cocoa for chocolate need lots of rain, so they grow in other countries and travel here.

learn.title: Food from the UAE
learn.text: UAE farms grow dates, tomatoes, lettuce and cucumbers. Fishermen catch fresh fish from our seas. This local food has only a short way to travel.

practice.title: The food journey
practice.prompt: Put the food's journey in order, from the farm to our table.

msc.goal: I can sort toys into old and new, and say how toys have changed.

learn.title: Toys long ago
learn.text: Long ago, children played with toys made of wood, cloth and metal. They did not need batteries or screens.

learn.title: Toys today
learn.text: Many new toys are made of plastic. Some need batteries, and some have screens.

learn.title: Then and now
learn.text: Old and new toys are both fun! But they are made in different ways.

learn.title: Still loved today
learn.text: Some toys are very old, but children still play with them today! Yo-yos, spinning tops, marbles, teddy bears and board games have been around for a long time.

learn.title: Long ago in the UAE
learn.text: Long ago in the UAE, many children made their own toys from things like palm leaves, sticks and cloth. They played lots of games outside with their friends.

practice.title: Old or new?
practice.prompt: Is it a toy from long ago, or a new toy?

practice.prompt: Match each toy to what it is made of.

more.title: Ask a grandparent
more.text: Ask a grandparent or older family member: What toys did you play with when you were 6? What were they made of? Tell them about your favourite toy too!
